results.name: expired JWT

results.expected: 401, zero side effects (no lifecycle, consent, closet, RPC or provider read)
results.sideEffects: only /auth/v1/user was called for the denied requests
results.limits: Stubbed Auth server: no live signed-JWT validation (same limit as 0737).

results.name: in-function auth with caller-controlled headers
results.input: seven identity headers + userId/user_id/actorId/ownerId body fields naming actor B with actor A token, on a B-owned anchor and an A-owned anchor; three schemaVersion smuggling values; a nested lookalike
results.expected: actor stays A (verified Auth); B anchor refused 403 with zero quota; unknown schema 400 before any read; no downstream call carries the B actor id
results.sideEffects: no RPC, provider or other-actor read for the refused requests
results.limits: Stubbed Auth server; ownership filter observed at the handler query (stub does not emulate RLS).

results.name: 10x declared body limit
results.input: unversioned: note 2,800 and 500,000 chars, 1,000 keepItems, 1,000 excludeItems, maximumOutfits 1e9, 2 MB unknown field; versioned: instruction 200/201/2,000/500,000, 500-char requestId, 21 candidates, a 2 MB unknown field, a non-string instruction
results.expected: every field bounded: note 280, keepItems 6, excludeItems 12, maximumOutfits 3, private instruction 200, private requestId 64; structural violations (21 candidates, unknown field, wrong type) 400 before quota/provider
results.sideEffects: structurally rejected private requests spend no quota and never reach the provider
results.limits: OBSERVATION: the unversioned path has no byte cap on the raw body (a 2 MB unknown field is parsed and ignored), and over-long text fields (unversioned note, private instruction and requestId) are silently TRUNCATED rather than rejected, so an oversize text request is served and spends quota. The request-size bound is the platform gateway. Not asserted as a defect.

results.name: Unicode homoglyph identifier

results.expected: identifier variants 400 with zero side effects; homoglyph ids from the provider never enter an outfit
results.limits: Tests the handler UUID allow-list and pool lookup; ids are never string-built into SQL (see 1137).

results.name: URL path traversal
results.input: six traversal/query-injection shaped anchor ids; seven inspiration rows with traversal, foreign-owner, encoded, absolute, wrong-extension, wrong-bucket and wrong-case storage paths
results.expected: 400 before any query for malformed ids; only the exact own-prefix .jpg row is a pool member; no Storage call
results.limits: The handler reads storage_path only as an eligibility predicate and never downloads it, so the real storage path guard (server download of an owned object) is not exercised.

results.name: SSRF metadata/local/file/gopher/DNS rebind
results.input: six SSRF-shaped URLs in event.note/occasion/dressCode/setting, anchor id, three unknown URL fields (unversioned) and instruction/context.occasion/candidate category+color (versioned); a hostile STYLE_OUTFIT_GEMINI_MODEL env value
results.expected: outbound hosts limited to the Supabase fixture and Gemini; no caller URL used as a request target; model path allowlisted
results.limits: The handler fetches only the fixed Gemini origin and Supabase; there is no server-side image or URL download in this function, so DNS-rebind against a fetched caller URL has no surface to test.

results.name: prompt injection per model field
results.input: delimiter-breaking injection in event.note (with a forged ANCHOR line and a forged closet line), closed-enum fields, user-authored closet and scan metadata (10 fields), private instruction/context.occasion; a model that obeys the forged anchor, an invented id and a role spoof
results.expected: no field changes the system prompt; closed enums drop the text; an obeying model still cannot place an out-of-pool or role-spoofed item in an outfit; private response limited to contract fields

perField.db:closet_subtype: present as data in the user turn only
perField.private.instruction/context.occasion: user turn only; response limited to contract fields; invalid occasion fails closed

results.limits: OBSERVATION: unlike stylechat-generate, the free-text prompt fields (event.note, user-authored closet/scan metadata) are NOT delimiter-escaped, so a newline can forge ANCHOR/closet lines in the user turn (shown: both lines present). Containment is the output validator, not input escaping. A provider-authored "reason" is returned bounded to 240 chars but otherwise unfiltered: a hostile or injected model could surface a URL or markup (shown: "Open http://evil.test/pay now x ```sql select 1```"). Proves prompt STRUCTURE and output containment only; whether a real model obeys needs a paid provider (excluded), as with 0749.

results.name: SQL injection per RPC parameter
results.input: SQL metacharacters + DROP TABLE payload in every body field (anchor type/id, keep/exclude, event.*, requestId, sessionId, userId, p_limit/dailyLimit/burstLimit overrides) on both branches
results.expected: no caller string is placed in any RPC parameter, URL or PostgREST filter; RPC bodies are exactly {p_limit: <server limit>}; table query shape unchanged
results.limits: The two RPCs take only an integer p_limit sourced from the server env, so the handler has no caller-controlled RPC string at all. The SQL bodies of check_and_increment_style_outfit_burst / increment_style_outfit_daily_usage are not exercised (needs a real Postgres).

results.name: MIME magic-byte mismatch
results.input: PNG bytes labelled image/jpeg and other image payloads in the unversioned request; image/storage fields on the versioned request
results.expected: image bytes never forwarded to the provider (unversioned ignored, versioned rejected 400 before quota)
results.sideEffects: no binary part in any provider request; no quota spent on rejected versioned requests
results.limits: ANALOG: this endpoint has no byte-upload path (text-only prompt; inspiration storage_path is an eligibility predicate and is never downloaded), so a magic-byte check has no surface here. Needs a ruling: PASS-scoped vs N/A by construction.

results.expected: never forwarded

results.name: 10 retries in 1 second
results.input: ten requests back-to-back (limiter stub allows 3 then denies); then malformed/errored limiter payloads, daily quota exhausted/malformed, and both denials on the versioned branch
results.expected: first 3 served, 7 denied 429 burst_limit, zero provider and zero daily-quota for denied; malformed or errored limiter fails closed; daily exhaustion 429; versioned branch identical
results.limits: Proves the handler honours the limiters. The limiters themselves are SQL (check_and_increment_style_outfit_burst, increment_style_outfit_daily_usage); not exercised. The 429 carries retryAfterSeconds in the body but no Retry-After header (client note).

results.limits: The function has no response/result cache of its own. Platform-level caching (CDN, gateway) is outside the handler and not exercised.

results.name: Supabase 401 mid-request
results.input: Auth succeeds, then each downstream read/RPC returns 401 JWT expired: closet, saved_scans, burst RPC, daily RPC (both branches), consent, lifecycle profile
results.expected: fail closed: no provider call, no further quota spend

profile (lifecycle) read 401.error: This account is scheduled for deletion.

results.sideEffects: zero provider calls in every variant
